note.p: We have not traced this reference. Yet the first use of the abbreviation is in 1795 and references remain sporadic until 1812, when they suddenly intensify. Godwin tends to iuse abbreviations for close intimates and members of the family. And once he starts to continue. These references seem to start out of the blue, and then fizzle out similarly, after dinning with Godwin in May 1814, and an invitation in January 1815, the next contact is his writing a letter in 1822. We believe these instancces of C M to be references to the same person, although there is one case in which he repeats the initials (2 March 1799)- although that may be a transcription error on Godwin's part when he writing up the diary). In 1812 the references seem to link CM with Mary Jane Clairmont - but he clearly knew CM long before he met Mary Jane.
